title: Docs: README, learning pages, guide, memory notes
description: Per designs/reorganization.md (sections: The sentence, Target layout, What is removed). Rewrite README.md around the sentence, the use case shape, and the check command, with the map of the six directories and the history below. Update learn/README.md, learn/guide.md, learn/proofs.md, learn/roles.md, learn/possession.md, and the hello step (now usecases/hello/README.md, linked from learn/) to the new paths and names: identities, responses, test-cases, engine, no core, no token file. Update the project's memory notes under the Claude memory directory that name moved paths.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green including the smoke test over every command line in the learning pages. No page mentions core/, callers/, records.json, or analysis/guardrails/.

title: History: snapshots and narratives under history/, link checker first
description: Per designs/reorganization.md (section: History). First write a link checker over every .html and .md in the tree (files and fragments) and a smoke test that runs every command line in learn/*.md and learn/hello, and make both part of check.sh (review finding 15). Then git mv the nine iteration directories (bola-reads, bola-writes, field-reads, field-writes, function-level, on-behalf-of, contract, row-filtering, gateway) under history/ with their names unchanged; move analysis/design.html to history/provable-composition.html and the narratives of iterations 11 through 15 and core/what-reservations-changed.html into history/; move the root index.html to history/index.html and put a one-page landing index.html at the root pointing at the README, learn/, and history/. Update the two cross-snapshot paths in history/gateway/test_interceptor.py and the orders parity tests in usecases/orders (test_build.py, test_interceptor.py) (review finding 16). Rewrite every link. Write history/README.md: what this is, the live code is elsewhere, and why the snapshot corpora keep positional reasons while the live ones use names.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green including the link checker and the smoke test. No iteration directory remains at the top level. Every snapshot still runs standalone with uv run --project history/<name> pytest.

title: The check command and check.sh
description: Per designs/reorganization.md (section: One command). cedar-osdc check DIR runs build, validate, run-tests, prove in order and stops at the first failure. validate uses the official cedar command when on the path, otherwise cedarpy.validate_policies; a missing cedar is not a failure (review finding 12). prove needs cargo and cvc5; when missing, check says so and stops. check.sh runs the engine's own tests, then check on usecases/hello, usecases/orders, usecases/reservations (a literal list), then prove-history.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green. cedar-osdc check usecases/reservations exits 0 on this machine, where cedar is not installed and cargo and cvc5 are. Each of the four steps is still callable alone.

title: Test case format: policies by @id name, export mapping, failure printout
description: Per designs/reorganization.md (section: Test cases). reason and errors in every test case under usecases/*/tests/test-cases/ name policies by their @id annotation instead of policyN (review finding 9); the corpus runner and the command line map names to positions; the --cedar-tests export maps them back to policyN. Add a test that every policy in every policies.cedar (use cases and snapshots) carries a unique @id. The rewrite script touches the live use cases only; the nine snapshots keep the positional format, and history/README.md (task 6) will say why. The per-file header stays. On a failure, run-tests prints the request on one line.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green. grep finds no "policy[0-9]" in usecases/*/tests/test-cases/. The uniqueness test exists and passes. Exported cedar run-tests files still carry policyN reasons.

title: Use case shape and proofs per use case
description: One task, because the analysis runner reads guardrails by their old paths and cannot be green between the move and the rewrite (review finding 1). Move usecases/orders, usecases/reservations, and learn/hello (which becomes usecases/hello) into the shape in designs/reorganization.md (section: The shape of a use case): contract/ with unity/, the ODCS document, and generated/; principals.cedarschema and actions.cedarschema at the root; guardrails/ moved from analysis/guardrails/<usecase>/ beside the policies; tests/ with test-cases/, identities/ (today callers/), responses/ (today records.json and records/; the descriptor's fetch reads tests/responses/<id>.json), events/, and the test_*.py files. Rebase the build's output keys for contract/ (engine/contract.py build() and the schema lookup in the command line). Give the runner its per-use-case mode, prove DIR: every file under guardrails/ is a no-op against the folder's policies, plus never-errors for every policy; and its chain mode, prove-history, reading the tables compiled into the runner with paths rewritten, policies from the snapshots and the live orders use case, schemas from history/chain/schemas/ for iterations 1 through 6 and the built schemas for the rest, guardrails from each snapshot's own guardrails/ and the live use cases. Create history/chain/ with schemas/, specs/, revisions/, restrictions/, and retired/ (the five retired files with their reasons); RETIRED becomes a list of (retired file, the final set it must differ from). Delete successor_of and the revised status (review findings 2 and 7 and the closing bug). Do not implement non-vacuity here.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green with the same 670 tests and 208 proofs (the proofs may be reported per use case and per chain, but every property proved before is proved after; list any that moved). uv run cedar-osdc prove usecases/hello runs (never-errors only) and its result is recorded in the task notes. The three retired reservations guardrails are still shown to fail against the final set in prove-history. No file remains under analysis/guardrails/, analysis/revisions/, analysis/restrictions/, analysis/specs/, analysis/schemas/.

title: Engine and interface split: engine/calls.py and the agreement test
description: Extract the tool call mapping from the Gateway handlers into engine/calls.py exactly as specified in designs/reorganization.md (section: The tool): a Call dataclass (action, resource, payload, context, row_id) and call(use_case, tool_name, arguments) raising ValueError for an unknown tool, an unusable id, an unexpected argument, or a partial set of presented facts. The engine's check_call and filter_object/filter_rows take a Call. The Gateway handlers build a Call from an event; the command line builds one from arguments; the command line stops reaching into the handlers' private methods (today cli.py uses handlers._context). Add the agreement test: for every request event and matching response event naming a governed tool, in every use case, the handler's translation and the command line's translation produce the same Call, CallDecision, and RowsDecision; engine values are compared, never printed words or Gateway envelopes (review finding 13).
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green. The agreement test exists, runs over orders, reservations, and hello, and passes. No import of gateway from cli or of cli from gateway. No behavior change: every existing test passes unmodified except for import paths.

title: Package skeleton: cedar_osdc with engine, cli, gateway
description: Create cedar_osdc/ with engine/, cli/, gateway/ per the layout in designs/reorganization.md (section: The tool). Move core/*.py into engine/ (claims.py becomes identities.py), core/cli.py into cli/main.py, the handler half of core/interceptor.py into gateway/handlers.py; add gateway/handler.py with the two Lambda entry points loading a use case by name. Update pyproject.toml (packages, console script cedar-osdc = cedar_osdc.cli.main:main), check.sh, the root conftest.py, and every import in usecases/, learn/hello, and the tests. Fix the two hard-coded parent paths: REPO in the command line and in its tests (review finding 3). Make the analysis runner take the repository root as an argument rather than deriving it from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, ready for prove DIR. The analysis crate and the bundled cvc5 stay where they are.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green (670 tests, 208 proofs) before and after. No file under core/ remains. uv run cedar-osdc run-tests usecases/reservations works from a fresh uv sync. git mv used for every move so blame survives.

title: Run 2: the use case shape, proofs per use case, the check command
description: The second overnight run of designs/reorganization.md: every use case in one folder shape with its guardrails beside its policies, the analysis runner proving one use case at a time and the history chain separately, test cases naming policies by @id, and cedar-osdc check. Depends on run 1.

title: Run 3: history, words, review
description: The third overnight run of designs/reorganization.md: the nine snapshots and every design narrative under history/, the link checker and command smoke test, the README and learning pages rewritten to the new layout, and a fresh review from a clean clone. Depends on run 2.

title: Run 1: package and engine split, no behavior change
description: The first overnight run of designs/reorganization.md: the cedar_osdc package with engine, cli, and gateway, and the extraction of the tool call mapping into the engine. Every check green before and after; no change to what any policy decides.

title: Non-vacuity check for guardrails, reporting only
description: Per designs/reorganization.md (section: Proofs per use case, review finding 6). For each guardrail and each request environment of the built schema, compare permit(principal, action, resource); alone against permit(principal, action, resource); plus the guardrail, and require a difference in at least one environment: some request satisfies the guardrail's scope and condition, so a misspelled level fails. Reuses the runner's difference check. Lands as reporting only: prove prints VACUOUS for a guardrail that changes nothing and does not fail. Record in the task notes which of the 27 live guardrails, if any, are reported vacuous; turning the report into a failure is a separate decision.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green. prove DIR prints a non-vacuity line per guardrail. The notes list the result for every live guardrail.

title: Review from a clean clone
description: A fresh reviewer with no context clones the repository, reads README.md, runs uv sync and the three commands the README gives, follows learn/README.md through step 1, and reports where the layout or the words lose them, with file and line evidence. Findings become follow-up tasks; nothing is fixed inside this task.
acceptance_criteria: A written report attached as notes on this task, ranked, with a concrete fix per finding.
